evidence.note: Establishes only a coarse view: common+storage=34 tests pass, api-server/others fail to compile. Repeatedly re-runs the same workspace test commands (155,157) without producing a consolidated failure list or per-binary counts.

A graveyard of near-identical re-runs of `cargo test --workspace`, all reporting the same frozen '34 tests pass'. No pass/fail deltas, no per-binary ledger; progress accounting is stalled for ~40 steps and misstates the target as '3000+' vs the actual 1,390.
Circular debugging on the Phase type (enum→struct→enum-with-consts→struct) never recognized as going in circles — evidence of failing to detect thrashing.
creation_timestamp flip-flops Option↔DateTime and the agent edits test files to compensate, showing loss of a stable ground-truth picture rather than tracked regression control.
Trajectory ends stuck ('terminal may be stuck'), still reporting 34 passing — no recovery, no accurate done-vs-remaining ledger across the 100 binaries.

reasoning: The agent runs tests frequently but never maintains a consolidated, current view of remaining failures: its count is frozen at '34 pass', it never enumerates per-binary status, misstates the total test count, and repeatedly re-issues identical commands without extracting deltas. It also fails to detect its own circular debugging (Phase type, timestamp flip-flops, brace hunts). This matches anchor 3 ('occasional ad hoc test runs with no consolidated view of remaining failures'), only marginally above it due to a crude compiles-vs-doesn't distinction, and well short of anchor 5's systematic working-down of a failing list.
